## 0.2.0 design system

Runtime API 3. A design system for productivity tools, separated from a neutral
runtime. The specification is in `docs/design/` (principles, atoms, composition,
themes, wireframes, decisions D1-D49); `docs/releases/0.2.0.md` has the
migration notes. Crate versions are still 0.1.8: the version bump and the
release follow separately.

28 commits, 355 files (+20,052 / -7,127).

### What changes

- **Neutral runtime and token base.** Themes are an open token registry;
  components declare the tokens and environment values they read and
  preparation validates them. The design language lives in
  `registry/tokens.rhai` (typography, spacing and relationship aliases,
  `metrics.*` in two densities, radius roles, derived colors); palettes carry
  colors only.
- **62 components rebuilt** on one set of contracts (size and density axes, one
  content inset, a 2px ink focus frame, four marker silhouettes, one tab stop
  per control).
- **Layouts and patterns**: Stack, Inline, Toolbar, Region; Section,
  DescriptionList, Stat, FormLayout, InlineState, DataView, ListDetail, AppShell
  with F6 regions.
- **Composition audit and profiles** (`composition_audit`, `gpui-rhai init
  --profile productivity`, `check` literal-geometry warnings).
- **The Gallery is a Rhai application** on AppShell: 83 pages, four keyboard
  scenes, a live audit count, a theme picker over every bundled theme, and
  square / subtle / round corner styles. On macOS its own TitleBar replaces the
  platform title bar.
- **Corner styles**: `corners` is an environment axis (`square` default,
  `subtle`, `round`); every radius role is zero when square, so square output is
  pixel-identical. Logical `radius_start` / `radius_end`.
- **Custom title bars**: `.window_drag_area()`, TitleBar/AppShell `window_drag`,
  inert unless the Host allows it (`ScriptViewConfig::window_drag_areas`,
  `ScriptApplication::window_drag_areas`).
- **Runtime diagnostics**: a failed transaction's error stays until a reload or
  a dismissal (banner Dismiss, `ScriptViewHandle::clear_error`) instead of
  vanishing on the next event; `gpui-rhai check` warns about entry functions
  that take over a built-in (`builtin-shadow`).
- **Performance**: definite widths for stretched children (Gallery frames
  20-52 ms to about 2 ms, pixel-identical), audits only after renders,
  copy-on-write `UiNode` (Rhai render time roughly halved).
- **Examples** rewritten with the 0.2 layouts and patterns; `byod_treemap`
  shows an application with its own design and no token base.

### Breaking changes

Listed in `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/releases/0.2.0.md`: runtime API 3, the token
base requirement, component prop/default changes (Button defaults to
`secondary`, Badge lamp, Card `variant`, removed row heights), Resizable's
`resize` payload is exactly the next `rect`, `last_error` keeps failures until
acknowledged, components that read radius tokens declare `corners`, and the
Rust Gallery shell is removed.

### Verification (local, macOS, at `c28849a`)

- `cargo fmt --check` in the workspace, `tests/native-keyboard` and
  `tests/performance`: pass.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` in the same three workspaces
  (workspace with `--all-features`): exit 0.
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --all-targets`: 677 passed, 0 failed.
- `tests/native-keyboard`: 235 passed, 0 failed (Gallery audit gate in both
  densities, keyboard scenes, tab-stop census, pointer tests, window drag
  areas).
- `tests/performance` (release): 2 passed, 0 failed.
- 57 visual baselines (Gallery 19 + examples 38) re-rendered offscreen and
  compared pixel by pixel: all identical; `scripts/audit-visual-baselines.sh`
  passes.
- The custom title bar was checked on a real window with posted mouse events:
  dragging the bar background moves the window, a drag that starts on a control
  does not.

Not run here: MSRV and release smoke; CI covers its own matrix.

### Known gaps

- The macOS window buttons sit about 1pt low in compact density (their position
  is fixed when the window opens).
- Window drag areas move the window on macOS and Linux; Windows is not handled.
- Double-click zoom on the custom title bar was not exercised on a real window.
